rowA.text: A · Mono — two numbers, one button

rowC.text: C · Orbit — native iOS, log from anywhere

rowD.text: D · Inbox — it finds them, you swipe

rowE.text: E · Calendar — the month at a glance

rowS.text: Shared by every direction — capture & AI

noteA.text:
Idea: the home screen is two big numbers (in, out) and one button. Nothing else competes.

Capture: hold the button and talk; let go to save. No confirm screen — an Undo toast instead.

Trade-off: the calmest and fastest to read. Categories and history sit one tap away.

noteB.text:
Idea: logging and asking are the same action — you message it.

Capture: talk, type ‘tapau nasi ayam 8’, or drop a screenshot. Every reply is an editable card.

Trade-off: the most flexible and the most ‘AI’. Long threads can get busy, so the month summary stays pinned on top.

noteC.text:
Idea: a native iOS 26 (Liquid Glass) app. One ring shows how much of what came in has gone out, split by category.

Capture: Lock Screen control, Action Button, Siri, widgets — log without opening the app.

Trade-off: the most polished on the platform. A ring is less exact than plain numbers.

noteD.text:
Idea: almost no typing. Apple Pay taps, screenshots and e-receipts land in an Inbox; you swipe to add them.

Rule: what you say is saved; what the app finds, you confirm.

Trade-off: the least effort per transaction, but it depends on one-time setup (a Shortcut, Photos access).

noteE.text:
Idea: time is the home screen. A heatmap shows which days cost the most; tap a day to see it or backfill it.

Capture: always aimed at a day, which suits ‘I forgot to log Sunday’.

Trade-off: the most informative over weeks; a little slower to read today’s numbers.
